prompt:
A 71-year-old retired teacher has 3 weeks of painless jaundice, dark urine, pruritus, pale stools, and 6 kg of unintentional weight loss. She was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 months ago and started on metformin. She is afebrile with stable vitals. Bilirubin 9.8 mg/dL (mostly direct), alkaline phosphatase 610, AST/ALT 140/180, INR 1.4. Ultrasound shows intra- and extrahepatic ductal dilation with a 14 mm common bile duct and a poorly visualized pancreatic head. The admitting team has booked ERCP with plastic stent placement for tomorrow and wants to send a CA 19-9 to 'confirm cancer.' What evaluation and sequencing would you recommend?

Provide a comprehensive management plan including appropriate diagnostic workup, referrals, procedures if indicated, follow-up, and actions to avoid.

rubric_items.text: Suspect a malignant distal biliary obstruction, most likely pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, given painless jaundice, weight loss, and new-onset diabetes.
Obtain a pancreas-protocol multiphasic contrast CT before any biliary stenting.
Refer early to a multidisciplinary pancreatic cancer team, including an HPB surgeon, before decisions about biliary drainage.
Obtain EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration or biopsy when a tissue diagnosis is needed, such as before neoadjuvant therapy or for unresectable disease.
Obtain chest CT to complete staging.
Defer preoperative biliary drainage if upfront resection can happen promptly and she has no cholangitis.
If biliary drainage is needed, place a self-expanding metal stent rather than a plastic stent.
Perform urgent biliary decompression if fever, rigors, or other signs of cholangitis develop.
Arrange surgery at a high-volume pancreatic surgery center if the tumor is resectable.
Offer germline genetic testing once pancreatic adenocarcinoma is confirmed.
Obtain MRI with MRCP as a complementary study if CT findings are indeterminate.
Measure CA 19-9 as a baseline marker, recognizing it can be falsely elevated by biliary obstruction and should be rechecked after decompression.
Assess performance status and nutritional status and involve a dietitian.
Give vitamin K for coagulopathy related to cholestasis.
Treat pruritus symptomatically, for example with cholestyramine.
Start pancreatic enzyme replacement if symptoms of exocrine insufficiency develop.
Discuss prognosis and goals of care as staging results return.
Assess venous thromboembolism risk and provide inpatient prophylaxis.
Monitor glucose closely and adjust diabetes therapy.
Send tumor molecular profiling if metastatic disease is found.
Provide return precautions for fever, rigors, or worsening abdominal pain.
Obtain PET-CT routinely for staging.
Perform staging laparoscopy before resection.
Send serum IgG4 to screen for autoimmune pancreatitis.
Attribute the jaundice to drug-induced liver injury from metformin and repeat liver tests in 4 weeks.
Refer directly to hospice without staging or a tissue diagnosis.
Proceed with ERCP and plastic stent placement before staging cross-sectional imaging.
Perform percutaneous CT-guided biopsy of a potentially resectable pancreatic head mass.
Use an elevated CA 19-9 to confirm a diagnosis of pancreatic cancer.
Use a normal CA 19-9 to exclude pancreatic cancer.
Refer for cholecystectomy for presumed choledocholithiasis without imaging the pancreas.
Delay cross-sectional imaging until the bilirubin normalizes.
Start high-dose glucocorticoids empirically for presumed autoimmune pancreatitis.
Perform a percutaneous liver biopsy to evaluate the cholestasis.
Proceed to exploratory laparotomy without staging imaging.
Order a HIDA scan to evaluate the jaundice.
Start empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics without signs of cholangitis.
Place a percutaneous transhepatic biliary drain as first-line drainage.
Order a noncontrast CT of the abdomen to evaluate the pancreas.
Tell the patient she definitely has cancer before imaging and tissue confirmation.
Order an upper GI barium series.
